nodes.summary: For every integer $g \ge 2$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n \equiv 1$ or $n \equiv 3 \pmod 6$ there is a Steiner triple system on the $n$ points $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which every set of $j$ distinct blocks, with $2 \le j \le g$, covers at least $j + 3$ points.
nodes.title: High-girth Steiner triple systems exist

nodes.summary: The statement that for every integer $g \ge 2$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n \equiv 1$ or $n \equiv 3 \pmod 6$ there is a Steiner triple system on the $n$ points $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (three-point blocks, every pair of distinct points in exactly one block) in which every set of $j$ distinct blocks, with $2 \le j \le g$, covers at least $j + 3$ points.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 207
